text:
The major product of the following reaction is –


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The substrate is ethyl 2-chloro-2-methylbutanoate, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3})(\mathrm{Cl})-\mathrm{COOC}{}_{2}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}$, a tertiary chloride.

With the strong base $\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{O}{}^{-}$ and heat, E2 elimination of HCl dominates over substitution at the tertiary carbon.

Removal of a β-H from the $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}$ of the ethyl group gives $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3})\mathrm{COOC}{}_{2}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}$ (trisubstituted), while removal from the methyl group gives $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}=\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{H}{}_{5})\mathrm{COOC}{}_{2}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}$ (disubstituted).

By the Saytzeff rule the more substituted alkene, ethyl 2-methylbut-2-enoate $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3})\mathrm{COOC}{}_{2}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}$, is the major product.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text:
The combination of plots which does not represent isothermal expansion of an ideal gas is – 


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For an isothermal process of an ideal gas, $PV_{m}=RT$ is constant, and $U$ depends only on $T$.

Plot (A): $P=RT\cdot \dfrac{1}{V_{m}}$ is a straight line through the origin, so it represents the process.

Plot (B): $P=\dfrac{RT}{V_{m}}$ is a rectangular hyperbola, not a falling straight line, so it does not represent the process.

Plot (C): $PV_{m}=RT$ stays constant as $P$ changes, a horizontal line, so it represents the process.

Plot (D): at constant $T$, $U$ stays constant as $V_{m}$ increases, so a rising $U$ versus $V_{m}$ line does not represent the process.

The plots that do not represent isothermal expansion are (B) and (D).

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th January Evening Slot

text: Molecules of benzoic acid $(C_{6}H_{5}$COOH) dimerise in benzene. 'w' g of the acid dissolved in 30 g of benzene shows a depression in freezing point equal to 2K. solution.body:
[IMG]

$\DeltaT_{f} = i K_{f}$ $\times$ $\frac{w}{M}\times \frac{1000}{w_{s}}$

i = 1 + $α\left (\frac{1}{n}-1\right )$

Here Benzoic acid dimerise, so value of n = 2

= 1 $-$ 0.4

= 0.6

text: If the de Broglie wavelength of the electron in $n^{th}$ Bohr orbit in a hydrogenic atom is equal to 1.5 $πa_{0} (a_{0}$ is Bohr radius), then the value of n/z is -
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
According to de Broglie hypothesis,

2$πr_{n} = nλ$

$\therefore$  $λ$ = $\frac{2πr_{n}}{n}$

According to the question, 

$\frac{2πr_{n}}{n}$ = 1.5 $πa_{0}$

We know,

$r_{n} = 0.529$ $\frac{n^{2}}{Z}$

    $= a_{0}$  $\times$ $\frac{n^{2}}{Z}$

$\therefore$  $\frac{2π}{n}\times \frac{a_{0}n^{2}}{Z}$ = 1.5 $π$ $a_{0}$

$\Rightarrow$  $\frac{n}{Z}$ = 0.75
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th January Evening Slot

text:
For a reaction consider the plot of $\ell$n k versus 1/T given in the figure. If the rate constant of this reaction at 400 K is $10^{–5} s^{–1}$, then the rate constant at 500 K is – 


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
From Arhenius equation,

K = Ae${}^{-\frac{Ea}{RT}}$

taking log both sides,

lnk = lnA $-$ $\frac{Ea}{RT}$

So in lnK vs $\frac{1}{T}$ graph

slope  = $-$ $\frac{Ea}{R}$

Rate constant at 400 K is $= 10^{-5} s^{-1}$

Let rate constant at 500 K is = K

$\therefore$   $\ln (10^{-5}) = \ln  A$ $-$ $\frac{Ea}{R(400)}$ . . . (1)

ln K = ln A $-$ $\frac{Ea}{R(500)}$ . . . .(2)

Subtracting (2) from (1) we get, 

ln $\frac{K}{10^{-5}}$ = $\frac{Ea}{R}$ $\left [\frac{1}{400}-\frac{1}{500}\right ]$

$\Rightarrow$   2.303 log $\frac{K}{10^{-5}}$ = 4606 $\left [\frac{1}{400}-\frac{1}{500}\right ]$

$\Rightarrow$   $K = 10^{-4} s^{-1}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th January Evening Slot

text: The correct order of atomic radii is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
N is a period-2 non-metal with a covalent radius of only about 70 pm, far smaller than the radius of any lanthanide, so N is the smallest.

Across the lanthanide series the atomic radius decreases steadily (lanthanide contraction), so Ce (183 pm) is larger than Ho (176 pm).

Eu is an exception to this trend. With the stable half-filled $4f^{7}$ configuration it gives only its two $6s$ electrons to metallic bonding instead of three, so the metallic bonding is weaker and its atomic (metallic) radius is anomalously large, about 199 pm, which is larger than that of Ce.

So the order of atomic radii is Eu > Ce > Ho > N.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th January Evening Slot
